content.text:
I was covering NN, Inc. (ticker NNBR). That came from the source record itself: the title "Why NN (NNBR) Is Up 24.7% After Pre-Selling New NVIDIA Liquid Cooling Capacity Expansion," the original_who field "NN, Inc.," and the source article's repeated references to "NN's" pivot, Wuxi plant, and Russell Microcap Value Index removal.

What the request explicitly said: the operating instructions set the task as one research record per question on a name you cover, with one source record to read against stored question pieces. The record named NN, Inc. The request did not name a ticker or company separately. It also contained no stored pieces, catalog entries, or linked questions, so I had nothing else to check the company identity against.

My inference: that the company under coverage is NN, Inc. That is a reasonable reading of the record, but it is inference, not an explicit instruction.

Two alternative readings I considered and rejected:

1. NVIDIA as the covered name. The record concerns NVIDIA's supply chain and its AI rack customers, so NVIDIA could be read as the subject. I rejected this because the announcing party, original_who, and the event are NN's own. NVIDIA appears as the customer, not the issuer of the claim, and the record makes no NVIDIA statement.

2. Multiple companies, with the Russell index and the 2028 projection figures treated as separate subjects. I considered treating the Russell Microcap Value Index, or the named analysts and the narrative projection provider, as separate covered entities. I rejected this because the source record ties the index removal and the projections to NN itself. The index is a market-structure event affecting NN's shares, and the projections are figures for NN's revenue and earnings. None of them introduces a different company.
